_comment: temper-io-types's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json,
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json, wasm_expected_failures_design_bundle.json,
wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json and
wasm_expected_failures_constraint_compiler.json. Same contract -- see
wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed
rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
This one is EMPTY, and that is a result rather than an omission: measured 2026-08-10
against 144 registered tests, all 144 execute and all 144 pass on
wasm32-unknown-unknown. What survives --no-default-features here is KiCad/DSN text
serialisation, footprint and S-expression parsing, provenance hashing, the DAG
expression parser and the placer CONTRACT kernels (Rect, netclass, manufacturing,
placement DRC, adjacency). None of them reads a clock, resolves a symbol through the
dynamic loader, draws entropy, or leans on a libm edge case, so none of the four
established divergence classes has anything to attach to.
Two things were specifically checked rather than assumed, because they are the
plausible wasm32 hazards in this crate:
- `dag_expr` recursion. `depth_boundary` drives a 996-frame `not` chain right up to
the MAX_DEPTH = 1000 ceiling and `tests::deep_nesting_is_bounded_not_overflowing`
pushes past it. wasm32's default 1 MiB shadow stack holds both: they pass, and the
module's peak linear memory across the whole run is 3.88 MiB.
- Float formatting. `pyfmt`, `dsn_types::format_dsn_arg` and
`dsn_exporter::py_format_fixed`/`py_round_half_even` pin CPython's round-half-even
and its lowercase nan/inf spellings. Those are Rust core-library formatting, not
libm, and agree bit-for-bit on wasm32 -- unlike temper-thermal's `hostmath`, whose
four expected failures come from `dlsym` being unavailable.
The file still exists because run_wasm_tests.mjs defaults to the temper-drc-rs
manifest, and pointing an io-types-only module at THAT one reports every drc entry as
an orphan exclusion and exits non-zero. Pass this file with
`--expected-failures tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_io_types.json`. It is also
where a future divergence gets recorded, so the shape is already right when one
appears.
An empty manifest is NOT a weaker gate. run_wasm_tests.mjs still fails the run on any
unexpected failure, so with nothing excluded here every one of the 144 tests is
load-bearing: a regression on wasm32 turns the step red immediately.
